title: Texans general manager discusses running game and rookie debut after Week 1
text:
Texans general manager discusses running game and rookie debut after Week 1
The Houston Texans' investment in their running game was evident in Week 1, general manager Nick Caserio said on Sept. 16 during an appearance on Texans All-Access.
Caserio said both David Montgomery and Woody Marks performed well sharing the load. "Both backs really ran well," Caserio said. "David ran well. Woody ran well." He highlighted Marks' efficiency with his touches, referencing both preseason performance and the most recent game: "Woody's really kind of maximized his touches," Caserio said. "You can go back to the preseason, the Vegas game — and in this game, I think he averaged five-plus yards a carry or whatever it was. So hopefully we can build on that."
Montgomery, acquired during the offseason along with other offensive reinforcements, provided head coach DeMeco Ryans with confidence in short-yardage situations. "There were some runs there. We kind of had these short-yardage situations where we had to get a yard or two — fourth-and-one, third-and-one," Caserio said. "And to be able to do that, DeMeco had confidence in the team's ability to do that, which is why we made the decision that we did."
Caserio also commented on broader trends across the league: "It's interesting when you look around the league — it's almost like we've seen a little bit of a shift in the running game," he said. He cited several teams surpassing 200 rushing yards recently and explained its importance for controlling games, Caserio said. "It enables you the ability to control the pace of the game to some degree, keep it in manageable situations. So overall, we did a decent job."
Rookie center/guard Keylan Rutledge's NFL debut was another topic discussed by Caserio: "Overall, he played pretty good football," Caserio said about Rutledge's first regular-season appearance for Houston. He added: "A lot of the things that we saw in the spring and in training camp, and even in the preseason — a small snapshot in the games that he played." On Rutledge's potential going forward: "He's a good football player. That's why we drafted him. He has a good playing style." While noting areas for improvement typical for rookies after their debuts, Caserio concluded: "Overall, he went in there and did a pretty good job against a pretty formidable front."
